unit.why: A single narrative: the Apta rabbi disguises himself to test a wonder-working tavern-keeper near Medzhybizh, who reveals that his power comes from trust in God and from taking God as his business partner.

stories.start_quote: ואכתוב מעשה ג' מה ששמעתי מאדם
stories.end_quote: ברכותיו והצלחתו עד בלי די אמן
stories.summary_en: The rabbi of Apta, disguised as a merchant, lodges with a tavern-keeper whose blessings always come true. He finds that the man splits every coin between two boxes. The man explains that in poverty he took God as his partner, gives God's half to the poor, and was rewarded with effective blessings. The rabbi blesses him and retells the tale ever after as a lesson in trust in God.
